**Inputs:** Ray origin $\mathbf{o}$, ray direction $\mathbf{d}$, triangle vertices $\mathbf{a}, \mathbf{b}, \mathbf{c}$.
**Outputs:** Boolean indicating intersection.
**Normal Calculation:** Compute the triangle normal $\mathbf{n}$.
**Plücker Coordinate Calculation:** Compute the Plücker coordinates for the three edges of the triangle relative to the ray direction.
**Winding Order Check:** Determine intersection based on the signs of $s_x, s_y, s_z$.
If the triangle vertices are ordered counter-clockwise relative to the ray, all Plücker coordinates will have the same sign.

**Memory Complexity:** $O(1)$ auxiliary space.
No additional data structures are required beyond the input vertices and ray.

The use of Plücker coordinates avoids the computation of barycentric coordinates during the intersection test, which can be faster than Möller-Trumbore if only the boolean result is needed [S7, unofficial].
However, if barycentric coordinates are required, additional computation is needed.
**Strengths:** Handles arbitrary ray directions.
Decouples intersection logic from plane geometry.
**Limitations:** Does not handle rays lying in the triangle's plane.
Requires front-face culling logic to be implemented separately if back-face intersection is desired.
**When to use:** When intersecting general rays against triangles and only the boolean intersection result is needed.
**When not to use:** When barycentric coordinates are required immediately (use Möller-Trumbore).
When rays are axis-aligned (use Axis-Aligned variant).
Plücker coordinates are a representation of lines in projective geometry, often used in computer graphics for efficient line-line and line-plane intersection tests.
